title: Product Comparison Video: Side by Side | AIVideosUGC
description: Make a product comparison video that puts two of your own colors, sizes, or models side by side. Get a 1:1 or 16:9 clip for your listing or Shorts. Try it.
h1: Make a Product Comparison Video of Your Own Options
lead: A product comparison video helps shoppers choose between your own colors, sizes, or models. Upload a photo of both, say what sets them apart, and get a short side-by-side clip.
intro: Two of your products stand next to each other so buyers can compare them at a glance. Our sample pairs a charcoal travel tumbler with a cream one on a light counter: same shape, different finish.

Comparison clips settle the small questions that hold up a sale, like which color, which size, or which lid. Use it for your own range only, such as two bottle capacities, a standard and a deluxe kit, or old packaging next to new. Pick 1:1 or 16:9 for a product listing, or 9:16 for YouTube Shorts. For a still comparison, use the Size Comparison template beside the clip.
tip: Shoot both products together in one photo, then spell out the difference in plain words, like "black tumbler on the left, cream on the right, same size."

steps.t: Upload both options in one photo
steps.d: Set the two products side by side on a plain surface so the video keeps them at the right scale.
Describe what sets them apart: color, size, lid, or finish. Use 6 seconds for a fast glance or 15 for a slow pan across both.
Add names, sizes, and prices above each product in Canva or CapCut after you download.

ideas.d: Stand your small and large bottles together so buyers see the real difference in height.
Show your updated design next to the previous one so returning customers recognize it.
Compare one item with your gift set to show exactly what the extra pieces are.

faq.q: Can I compare my product with another brand's?
faq.a: No. Use this template to compare options from your own range, like two colors or two sizes. Requests that include other companies' logos or trademarks may be refused.

faq.q: Can the video show capacity, weight, or price?
faq.a: Add specs like these as text in your editor after downloading. Generated numbers aren't always accurate, so it's safer to type them yourself.

faq.q: Which aspect ratio should I choose?
faq.a: Square 1:1 works well in product galleries and feeds. Widescreen 16:9 suits a video in your product description. Vertical 9:16 is for YouTube Shorts and other phone-first feeds.
